title: Implication, Converse and Contrapositive
quickIdea: p -> q is false only when p is true and q is false. Its contrapositive not q -> not p is equivalent to it; its converse q -> p and its inverse not p -> not q are not.
remember: Implication p -> q is false in exactly one row: p true, q false. That row is the whole truth table.
Vacuous truth: when p is false, p -> q is true whatever q is.
Converse of p -> q is q -> p. Inverse is not p -> not q. Contrapositive is not q -> not p.
Only the contrapositive is equivalent to the original. Converse and inverse are equivalent to each other, not to the original.
English map: 'p only if q' = p -> q; 'p if q' = q -> p; 'p unless q' = not q -> p; 'p when q' = q -> p; 'q is necessary for p' = p -> q; 'q is sufficient for p' = q -> p.
Biconditional p <-> q is (p -> q) and (q -> p); it is true exactly when p and q agree.

example.prompt: Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of 'if it is raining then the ground is wet', and say which is equivalent to it.
example.work: Converse: if the ground is wet then it is raining. Inverse: if it is not raining then the ground is not wet. Contrapositive: if the ground is not wet then it is not raining.
example.answer: Only the contrapositive is equivalent to the original. The converse fails when the ground is wet for another reason.

gateAngle: Two shapes recur. Translation: 'fail grade cannot be given when the student scores more than 50%' is q -> not p (2024 Set 2 Q.12, official key). Naming: 'converse of I stay only if you go' is 'I stay if you go' (1998 Q.1.5).

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Write the contrapositive of 'if a graph is a tree then it has no cycle', and state whether it is equivalent to the original.
variations.answer: If a graph has a cycle then it is not a tree - equivalent
variations.why: The contrapositive swaps and negates both parts: not (no cycle) -> not (tree). Swapping and negating both sides preserves truth in every row, so the two are equivalent.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How many of the four rows of p -> q and q -> p differ?
variations.answer: Two rows: (p, q) = (true, false) and (false, true)
variations.why: Both are true at (true, true) and (false, false) and both are false in the swapped rows. Two differing rows is exactly why the converse is not equivalent.

trap.what: Assuming the converse, or treating 'only if' as 'if'.
trap.why: p -> q says nothing about what happens when q is true. Using the converse is the single most common lost mark in this topic.
trap.counterexample: 'If a number is divisible by 4 then it is even' is true. Its converse, 'if a number is even then it is divisible by 4', fails at 6. Yet its contrapositive, 'if a number is odd then it is not divisible by 4', is true.

check.question: 'I stay only if you go.' What does that forbid?
check.answer: It forbids 'I stay and you do not go'.
check.explanation: P -> Q is false only in the row P true, Q false. So staying while you do not go is the one situation the assertion rules out.
